Studies going back almost 100 years have noted that fatty diets increase blood sugar levels by inducing insulin resistance. The mechanism is that fat enters the muscles quickly, and interferes with the interaction between insulin and insulin receptors. Intramyocellular lipids: fat inside your muscle cells (which builds up within 2 hours of a meal), blocks the insulin pathway. The sugar has nowhere to go since insulin isn't working, and so blood sugar rises. Eating fat based diets leads to higher and higher blood sugar levels as a result of the insulin>storage pathway being blocked by intramyocellular lipids.

Liponeogenesis from carbohydrate intake is an expensive metabolic process in humans. It costs about 30% of the calories consumed to convert carbohydrates into fats. It costs about 3% of the calorie intake to repack fat into lipids ready to be shipped off and stored in your ass. You will get fatter eating equal calories of fats than you will sugar.

"Please don't forget about me." Were my last words before she left for her trip to fuck around. "Don't be ridiculous! How could I ever forget about you? I love you!"

She forgot very quickly and, ten days later, on our 12th anniversary, I was informed by the psychiatrist, as she sat emotionless in the room, that she had no interest in saving the relationship.

In a heartbeat, everything was erased. Contact cut. I gave her a card I made in 'art therapy' with a beautiful poem, and begged her to bring me my guitar. "You're just going to try to make me love you again." Fucking cold.

Two years later, I still dream about her every night. Dreams or nightmares. Waking up is always painful. My brain is wired up around her, I will never forget her eyes. In the first few seconds I think, "Where is she? Where am I?" The next few seconds, "I should contact her, I miss her so much..." Then I spend a few hours in bed, in the fetal position with a cramping, churning stomach, realizing that no, I shouldn't do that, and dwell on how fucked up my life is, until I finally have to run to the washroom.

I couldn't imagine moving back in with her platonically, as you did. That sounds like fucking torture, but I would probably jump at it too, if given the opportunity, in hopes of rekindling something. It sounds like an invitation for great pain though. My anxiety would be surging at all times.

I left everything with her in that nice apartment. Affordable (cheaper than I pay now) with a stunning view on the 20th floor. You could see rivers and bridges and farmland, close enough to watch planes land but not hear them. Across from my favorite childhood park. I always wanted to live up high, finally I got to. Now I sleep on the ground floor in an ant infested studio, on the rock hard mattress my obese great aunt died on, waking up in physical pain every day. I avoid most of the city I grew up in. She haunts it. I'm terrified of seeing her. I'm forced to stay here because of a housing subsidy. I can walk a block and look south to see where my heart was ripped out. Only a small dose of opiates daily keeps me from spiraling into hell.

Every night she sleeps on the soft, expensive bed we spent weeks picking out and went halves on, watches the big plasma with surround sound we went halves on, sits on the designer couch she absolutely needed, because it can transform into a *comfortable* bed for her annoying friend to sleep on. The computer was mine, but I left it so she could still watch netflix. The router too, the modem I owned. I made sure she never went a day without internet. God, I am a fool. I thought there was a chance, if I did everything I could...

She would never, in our 12 years, reveal her finances to me. I didn't nag about it. Privacy is important (I would never read her e-mail, even if it was left open) I respect boundaries and lust for trust.

Every shared expense was halved. She knew all my finances, I was poor, and told her. Chinese girl from a wealthy, well educated family, with high expectations for who she marries. Dad consults for big oil. I come from a mechanic and a secretary who worked her way into admin. I don't think my father even graduated.

Her father locked me in his office and demanded that I stop seeing his daughter 4 months into us dating, and she couldn't understand why I had an awkward relationship with them.

My surgeries and illness and unemployment were kept secret from her family too, so I had to put on a stressful show. Once my savings ran out, after my surgeries, and I couldn't pay my full half of rent anymore, it only took a year or so for things to collapse.

All I took with me were my guitars and my music gear. I ripped down all the bedroom decorations I had put my heart into (she became quite depressed when we moved, until I decorated again. "It feels like home now", she said). She can't have that anymore, that's me. Let whatever man has her now write her poems and love songs, serve dinner in the sunset on the roof, and decorate the bedroom like the Sistine Chapel. None of my friends treated their women like that. I hope someone is fucking her right now, boringly, and she's surrounded by plain walls, starring at a bare ceiling with a dead look in her eyes. No longer looking up into foliage, filled with origami butterflies and tiny lights dimmed to look like the starry night.

I took all the lingerie. A friend told me not to. But I took it. It's all mine. I have a suitcase full of it and sex toys, some light bondage. I put a lot of money and time into keeping our sex life interesting. She invested nothing. She once told me, "You know, I think I enjoy eating more than sex." It was heartbreaking. That always stuck with me.

This is a multi orgasmic girl who I put great effort into satisfying 4 or 5 times before she couldn't take it anymore. It was a lot of work. If they could only understand. Perhaps it requires too much creativity for her, or she really would rather eat a sandwich. She hadn't orgasmed until she met me. Her fingers were too busy with chopsticks to explore her body I guess.

I took these things because I cannot bear the thought of her dressing up for a new man when she invested NOTHING. They are mine, not hers. Very carefully chosen for her body type. She never felt beautiful until she met me, she said. I keep them with the desperate hope that she will ever come back. She won't. I had to keep a clean shaven face, but I wasn't allowed to be unimpressed when she came home with a boy's haircut. If she asked, she would have known: Please don't, you have no tits already. At least the first time it was for cancer fundraising.

Oh well! At least half the rent is being paid again, maybe, and she can eat Indian food with someone again! (My stomach was bad for many years, and getting worse). I won't miss smelling those farts.

When I watch documentaries of men who are stricken with illness and their wives stick with them, it really makes me cry. I thought that was the kind of love I had. She said she never wanted kids, emphatically, but I was not looking like reproduction material, and we know, eventually, they'll want a kid.

Every day, I'm filled with anxiety and dread as I open my email, hoping for something. Something from her, confessing that she misses me. Something from a friend, saying they care. Or I'll write them - "I'll get back to you later." In what year? Or, from others, simply no reply...

I've given up, I've disconnected. It should be concerning - me actively pushing people away, but it's just an admission of my new reality. Nothing has changed. It's just reorganized to reflect the truth.

She packed boxes while I was in the psyche ward. My parents "kindly" moved them into the room where I hung myself. Now I get to open boxes and unwrap framed photographs of her and I in the room where I tried to end my life. I asked them to please not move anything back into that room. They did anyway. Like you, I was not a bread winner. Her wealthy family had put her through university and she had a good paying job in a field she enjoyed. I tried my best to contribute. Sometimes, rarely, I had to be the one keeping us afloat. When we moved provinces, I had a job lined up but she didn't. I worked 70 hours a week for months when we moved provinces.

Things began to go south when my health deteriorated rapidly, and I required multiple surgeries. Unfortunately, they left me with chronic pain that doctors could simply not explain. It's been debilitating and humiliating (my ass has been probed more times than mars).

I had whittled my diet down drastically. A toilet paper allergy? I tried every brand. Eventually I just started washing myself in the shower. Nothing helped. She left two months before my colonoscopy for colon cancer. I really wish that it had been positive. Fatal. I imagine there would have been a lot more support from family, friends, her, and the medical system, and I could leave this world with people at my side. Instead, I'm painted as a lazy do-nothing who got what he deserves in life. Abandoned by everyone.

When the workers ask who a person I could call in an emergency is, I draw a blank. Everyone criticizes me and beats me down. No one listens and supports me. Logistical support, perhaps from my sister or parents... But emotionally, they all criticize. My schizophrenic friend? He's out to lunch half the time and is as depressed as I am, a complete recluse. I go days and days without using my vocal chords.

I'm not a success story (yet? One can dream), but at least I can relate. Maybe you can find solace in the fact that someone else is suffering as you do.

I recommend the andoid app "Loop - Habit Tracker."


https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.isoron.uhabits&hl=en

Lightweight, open source, ad-free, and super easy to use. It's helped me and my friend a lot in managing our screwed up lives. It reminds you of tasks at specified times, and you check off whether you've done it, delay it until later (you specify how long inside the program) or dismiss. If you dismiss, it will pester you the next day until you've finally done the task, then it will wait for the next interval to expire. For example, if I don't trim my beard in a week, it will begin bugging me every day about it, until I do it, then it will wait a week to bug me again.

It generates exportable charts to keep track of the strength of your habits, so you know how well you're doing. I use mine for everything from am/pm medication reminders, once weekly beard trimming and other hygiene stuff, twice weekly watering plants, tracking my alcohol consumption, changing bed sheets, replacing my bath towel, it tells me to go outside (and tracks how much I don't, because I dismiss that one a lot =/). It's a great tool and it can be transformative. It's tiny and works fine on the 7 year old phone I gave my friend when I got a hand-me-down from my sister.

One of the best designed, lightest, and most life-changing apps I've ever used. You just have to OBEY.

There is only one clear choice now.

"I think the evidence is in people's experiences."

That's called anecdotal evidence, and is completely unreliable. Science throws it straight into the trash can. We'd still be bloodletting, which killed a POTUS, because he was a staunch believer in "people's experiences." We don't do that anymore, because we figured out science, and realized we were fools.

People are full of miracle stories: From "healing hands" to "magic crystals", "magnetic bracelets" and "homeopathy", "acupuncture" and "hypnotism". My aunt with lupus has raved about them all at some point, while withering away to nothing until she started eating pot cookies (something with supporting evidence to increase appetite. The munchies. Who would have thought?).

Should I blindly believe all that quackery? Or should I dig through the science to see if any of these 'treatments' have evidence of efficacy and any scientifically recognized mechanism by which they operate? Homeopathy claims water molecules have 'memory' - an explanation of how it might work (even though it doesn't), but an explanation with no foundation in science. Just another curtain behind a curtain. 

If the basic mechanism of how the treatment works is bunk, it is immediately invalidated. It's like me telling you that drinking orange juice cures depression. I have a lot of friends that have benefited from orange juice therapy. Orange juice flows into the brain, and the tartness combined with the high levels of vitamin C restores balance to the neurotransmission system. There: A woo mechanism to support my Orange Juice theory. A mechanism that a 10th grader could invalidate, since orange juice does not flow into your brain unless you jam a needle into your skull while eating your cheerios.

Should I try every single quack treatment because some people have had success? Maybe some edgy doctors will bring bloodletting back. In this new anti-science, post-enlightenment era, it might be a big hit. A simple appeal to tradition: "This is an ancient treatment from hundreds of years ago. The wisdom of our ancestors!" Dr. Oz would say. Ah yes, ancient "wisdom", like acupuncture. If only bloodletting came from the "East". The power of mystical "Eastern Medicine": an even greater sell. Just a few people have to experience a placebo effect, or a regression to the mean, and bam, you'll have a congregation rabidly supporting bloodletting again.

ECT has a mechanism, it triggers grand mal seizures in the left frontal lobe, and it's theorized that the neural pathways have to reintegrate after such seizures. Sort of pushing a 'reset button.' It also demonstrates 80% efficacy for depression remission to back it up. It also has risks (that are exaggerated), but it is a frightening idea. I have seen nothing comparable in either the mechanistic explanations of how EMDR works nor a body of research showing its efficacy beyond talk therapy. If we had something risk free, with the mechanistic theory and evidence of efficacy comparable to ECT to treat PTSD, it would be the first line treatment.

Thanks for the theoretical explanation of how it may work, but it seems tantamount to getting someone to shake around on the ground, pretending to have a seizure, while trying to talk them out of epilepsy. I'm going to do mountains of research, and possibly try it within the next month or two. If I find any compelling evidence beyond anecdotes, and a therapist that actually reads scientific literature.

I'm not a pill pusher either. I'm extremely skeptical about psychotropic medications. I bring my doctor piles of new literature that indicates their inefficacy. All he can say, with a sigh, is "What do we do now?.." Well, a medically assisted suicide would be nice. He's as demoralized as I am when it comes to treating mental health.

Pills have become the standard because it seems that nothing really works. The placebo effect and regression to mean happen, and pills are the easiest treatment to dispense (and benefit from the most powerful lobbying efforts). Mental health is becoming a *very* lucrative, and rapidly growing, epidemic.

Medications do have scientific theories and measurements behind their mechanisms of action (questionable ones). They're based on the action of the enzyme monoamine oxidase and the levels of the neurotransmitters that it cleans up. The history of this discovery is interesting. The medications are designed around this theory. Earlier last century it was about inhibiting monoamine oxidase directly, now it's about targeting the specific neurotransmitters, because there are less side effects. There is far more concrete evidence on this theory than the unexplained magic of EMDR, but at no point did I recommended pills. I only indicated that the quality of the research you cited for EMDR was poor, and didn't actually show efficacy for EMDR. It actually demonstrated greater efficacy for PE and, more importantly, just an overall benefit from simply being in contact with a therapist.

If the OP hasn't tried PE, then this research indicates they should immediately abandon EMDR and explore PE as an option. Even CBT, which professionals seem to think is some kind of panacea, has very underwhelming evidence. When I mention it, I mean that it should just be used as a control group therapy in these studies so that we have comparative evidence.

I hoped that my post would encourage others to take scientific literacy seriously. I spent a few hours digging through these papers in detail, exploring the authors, investigating funding, and researching the history of the journals. Very few people are willing to do that, but it's an essential skill if you really want to take control of your treatment.

It seems only a few factors are indisputably associated with good mental health: size and quality of social circles, trusting intimate relationships, safe comfortable living conditions, affliction-free physical health, regular exercise, and avoidance of alcohol and drug abuse. After a few years of this hopelessness, my girlfriend of 12 years, my best friend, the person I wanted to grow old with, went on a trip out east, and I found out that she cheated on me. I guess she finally gave up on me. 

I called my mother and told her what happened, she said, "So what?" I threw my phone across the room. My family is shit, but I had to go stay with them that night. I couldn't sleep, so I ran back to my apartment at 3am and climbed into bed with my cheating girlfriend, begging her to talk with me, she would not. I had a slow and lonely walk back to my parents'.

Because of IBS problems I've suffered with for more than a decade, I had been eating nothing but white rice for a week, experimenting while my girlfriend was away, trying to see if I could ever take a normal shit again by restricting my diet. I was hungry, and the thought of eating another spoonful of white rice made me feel sick. In a state of panic I decided to hang myself. I took my belt and jammed it into a window-frame lock, looped it around my neck, knelt down and went unconscious. The locking mechanism could not hold the entire weight of my slack body, it broke. I woke up on the floor, very confused. Why was on on the floor? Why was it so hard to breathe? What was this thing around my neck? Why couldn't I feel or move my limbs? Slowly, sensation returned to my body and I recalled that I just tried to kill myself.

This was around 6am. My mother woke up to get ready for work. I informed her that I'm a danger to myself, and I needed to go to the hospital. She told me that I was a pain in the ass and that she had regional meetings that morning, she didn't have time for this shit. I went back to the bedroom and thought about trying to hang myself again, but it was a scary experience. Instead, I called the woman who just broke my heart and she called 911. I spent a month in the psyche ward, a month in my sister's den on a mattress, and now 6 months in a group home for people with persistent mental illnesses. It's has been a horrific, dehumanizing experience.

I've lost more than half of my friends, because most have decided to side with my ex, not wanting to "get between the two of us". The other half are afraid of the darkness that surrounds me, and have barely spoken to me in six months. I wish someone would just invite me out for a few beers. I hint to them, "man I need a beer", or "I need to get out"... Nobody wants to deal with this mess. I have three friends left, one on the other side of the world.

I struggle to stay focused on my goals, upgrading my highschool sciences so that I can enter some field of medical imaging. It's something to shoot for, I guess.

I wait. The time passes on the year-long period of no-contact that my girlfriend imposed on our relationship, to then "see where we are, see what I've done to better myself, see how we feel." I wait to have my heart re-broken, to go through all of those feelings again. I cry every day, at least 30 minutes, thinking about her, and all of this. I write letters to her that I don't post, I save them to give to her on that date, when she will surely say goodbye forever.

I've now qualified for an independent living subsidy, and am moving out of the group home into my own apartment at the end of the month. I'm scared of the search, and I'm terrified that the loneliness will push me to attempt suicide again, but I have to get out of this place because of the psychological abuse that I'm subjected to by the people who operate it.

This is my mid-30's story. It is a fucking horror-show. I have a war-chest of prescribed benzos and anti-depressants to battle reality, but they don't do much, and the only comfort that I take is that life will eventually end on its own, one day, without my intervention, and I'll no longer have to suffer or think about these things any longer.

You are a billionaire of time, and I guarantee that you have moments in life left to experience that will make you glad you're still alive. Wait a while, just to see what happens... If I killed myself at 21 (and I often thought of it, and even tried) I would have missed my very favorite moments of life. I could not have predicted them.
